```{r}  
library(fpp2)

TOTALNSA <- read.csv("TOTALNSA.csv")

TOTALNSA_ts <- ts(TOTALNSA$TOTALNSA,
                  start = c(1976, 1),
                  frequency = 12)


TOTALNSA_ts <- window(TOTALNSA_ts, start = c(2008, 1))

# Examine the updated dataset
head(TOTALNSA_ts)
plot(TOTALNSA_ts)
# The dataset displays monthly vehicle sales beginning in January 2008.

TOTALNSA_diff1 <- diff(TOTALNSA_ts, differences = 1)

plot(TOTALNSA_diff1)
tsdisplay(TOTALNSA_diff1)
#The plots help determine whether trends remain after differencing.

auto_fit <- auto.arima(TOTALNSA_ts,
                       trace = TRUE,
                       stepwise = FALSE)

auto_fit
attributes(auto_fit)
#selects an ARIMA model for vehicle sales based on the data.
plot(forecast(auto_fit, h = 15, level = c(99.5)))
#The selected ARIMA model forecasts vehicle sales for the next 15 months. The shaded region represents the 99.5% prediction interval, showing uncertainty around the forecast.
Acf(auto_fit$residuals)

Box.test(residuals(auto_fit), lag = 20, type = "Ljung")

plot.ts(residuals(auto_fit))

hist(auto_fit$residuals)

tsdiag(auto_fit)
#Residual analysis evaluates whether the ARIMA model has captured the important patterns in vehicle sales.
plot(TOTALNSA_ts)

nsdiffs(TOTALNSA_ts)

ndiffs(TOTALNSA_ts)

ndiffs(diff(TOTALNSA_ts, 12))

tsdisplay(diff(diff(TOTALNSA_ts, 12)))
# Seasonal differencing compares vehicle sales with the same month of the previous year to help remove recurring seasonal patterns.
fit3 <- auto.arima(TOTALNSA_ts,
                   trace = TRUE,
                   stepwise = FALSE)

fit3
#This model automatically identifies an appropriate ARIMA structure, including seasonal terms when supported by the data.
Acf(fit3$residuals)

Box.test(residuals(fit3), lag = 20, type = "Ljung")

plot.ts(residuals(fit3))

hist(fit3$residuals)

dev.off()
par(mar = c(4, 4, 2, 1))
tsdiag(fit3)
```
